calculation_checks.lesson_anchor: Wave quantities and phase > Displacement and amplitude > Worked Example 1: Determining displacement and amplitude
calculation_checks.independent_check: Peak at +6.0 mm and trough at -6.0 mm gives peak-to-peak 12.0 mm; amplitude = 12.0 / 2 = 6.0 mm; instantaneous displacement at that instant = +3.5 mm.

calculation_checks.lesson_anchor: Wave quantities and phase > Period and frequency > Worked Example 2: Calculating frequency from timing data
Wave quantities and phase > Wavelength and wave speed > Worked Example 3: Identifying wavelength from crests and troughs
calculation_checks.independent_check: Separation between crest and adjacent trough is lambda / 2 = 1.00 m - 0.40 m = 0.60 m; lambda = 2 x 0.60 m = 1.20 m.

calculation_checks.lesson_anchor: Wave quantities and phase > Reading wave graphs: space versus time > Worked Example 4: Extracting wave quantities from dual graphs
calculation_checks.independent_check: Graph 1: lambda = 6.0 cm - 2.0 cm = 4.0 cm = 0.040 m; amplitude = 3.0 mm. Graph 2: T = 5.0 ms - 1.0 ms = 4.0 ms = 4.0 x 10^-3 s; f = 1 / 0.0040 s = 250 Hz.

calculation_checks.lesson_anchor: Wave quantities and phase > What is phase? > Worked Example 5: Determining phase relationships
calculation_checks.independent_check: P (y = 0, upward) and Q (y = 0, downward) have opposite velocity vectors, so they are in antiphase (180 degrees). P and R (y = 0, upward, separated by 1 lambda) have identical displacement and direction, so they are in phase (0 or 360 degrees).

calculation_checks.lesson_anchor: Wave quantities and phase > Quantitative phase difference > Worked Example 6: Phase difference from spatial separation
calculation_checks.independent_check: Delta x / lambda = 0.20 m / 0.80 m = 0.25. Delta phi in degrees = 0.25 x 360 degrees = 90 degrees; in radians = 0.25 x 2 pi rad = pi/2 rad approx 1.57 rad.

calculation_checks.lesson_anchor: Wave quantities and phase > Quantitative phase difference > Worked Example 7: Phase difference between two wave traces
calculation_checks.independent_check: Delta t = 0.25 s - 0.15 s = 0.10 s; T = 0.60 s. Fraction = 0.10 / 0.60 = 1/6. Delta phi in degrees = (1/6) x 360 degrees = 60 degrees; in radians = (1/6) x 2 pi rad = pi/3 rad approx 1.05 rad.

learning_design.rationale: 7 visuals support the physical progression: historical Weber wave channel apparatus, spatial wave snapshot dimensions, temporal displacement-time trace, authentic Paper 2 spatial grid (Fig. 4.2), authentic Paper 2 dual-wave time grid (Fig. 7.2), circular phasor phase mapping, and authentic Paper 1 period identification (Fig. 20). 6 selectable activities verify comprehension of core develop and explain concepts without text typing requirements, featuring per-option feedback addressing common candidate misconceptions.

notes: Verified controlled definitions 9702_def_amplitude, 9702_def_period, 9702_def_frequency, 9702_def_wavelength, and 9702_def_displacement match definitions.json verbatim, including Cambridge-accepted alternative descriptions of wavelength.

Verified controlled formula 9702_formula_period_frequency (T = 1/f, f = 1/T) and phase difference relations (Delta phi = Delta x / lambda * 360 deg or 2 pi rad; Delta phi = Delta t / T * 360 deg or 2 pi rad) against formulas.json.

Verified first-principles physical mechanisms: distinction between localized particle oscillation and overall wave disturbance propagation; dual representations (displacement-distance frozen snapshot giving spatial wavelength lambda vs displacement-time particle history giving temporal period T); amplitude as maximum displacement from equilibrium line vs peak-to-peak distance (2A); criteria for in-phase motion (matching displacement AND matching velocity direction) vs antiphase motion (opposite displacement and velocity, Delta phi = 180 deg or pi rad); wave propagation speed vs variable particle speed.

Independently recalculated all 7 worked examples (WE1 to WE7), verifying numerical precision, unit consistency, metric prefixes (mm, cm, ms), and separation of formal numerical Answer from conceptual Explanation.

Independently solved all 6 activities (A01 to A06), confirming correctness of answer keys ('A' for each) and pedagogical validity of all distractor feedback branches addressing common candidate errors (peak-to-peak confusion, reciprocal period-frequency inversions, axis misinterpretation, opposite velocity phase trap, dimensionless fraction without angle conversion, and frequency vs phase difference).
